    Lemma 9.3: two-sided factor paths #

    integral-partial-lifts.tex (lem:two-sided-factor-paths): "let b be a two-sided ray. If s has type L and bs is nonzero and shiftable, then every ordinary path representing b consists of two-sided arrows. Dually, the same conclusion holds if r has type R and rb is nonzero and shiftable."

    The proof of the first-arrow form (first_TB) uses only that the left factor is not an identity, so every nonidentity left factor of b is two-sided (leftFactor_TB). For an ordinary path a₁ ⋯ aₙ of b (IsOrdPath), all prefix products are therefore two-sided; an arrow aᵢ between two two-sided prefixes has both endpoint actions nonzero, since a two-sided ray commutes with q̂, so it is two-sided (ordPath_TB). The dual statement follows by passing to Sys.op (ordPath_TB').
